data.narrative:
Aclarity is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Julie Bliss Mullen that has raised $14M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes one public comparable (Linzagolix, ticker LNZA) and eight private peers, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tiers to support a median-based approach—only zero narrow-filter matches were identified despite nine total sector peers.

Consequently, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Using the $14M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields an implied value of $28M. This method assumes capital raised serves as a reasonable floor and that the company's next funding round will command the standard cross-stage expansion multiple observed in comparable-stage financings.

The triangulated analysis, derived from this single applicable method, supports a valuation range of $24M to $32M, with a median of $28M. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight peer comparables (which would narrow and validate the range), execution risk inherent to the seed-to-Series-B progression, and sector-specific capital availability in Climate & Energy. Given reliance on a single methodology, wider sensitivity testing around stage multipliers (1.5x to 2.5x) would strengthen conviction.
